long_biography.plain_text:
Kjell Inge Røkke left formal schooling for fishing and moved to the United States at 21. After buying a 69-foot trawler in 1982, he expanded into a global fisheries enterprise. His RGI vehicle became Aker’s largest shareholder in 1996 and later merged with Aker, giving him control of an industrial investment group spanning energy, technology, real estate and marine biotechnology.

Røkke remains Aker’s chair and controls 68.2 percent through TRG. His later ocean work gives the maritime story a different purpose: he joined the Giving Pledge in 2017 and funded REV Ocean, a not-for-profit initiative whose 195-metre vessel is designed as shared research infrastructure for scientists, policymakers and innovators. It brings nine laboratories, deep-sea robotics and submersible access together for collaborative ocean missions.
